description: ATmega2560 <-> ESP8266 line protocol: encode cases (Frame -> exact bytes) and decode cases (bytes -> Frames or errors). Read by src/iot/court-box/test/test_protocol. Checksums here were produced by an independent Python XOR, not by the codec under test.

encode.note: A caller asking for 16 hours gets the 90-minute hard cap, not a rejection.
Zero seconds would be an indefinite-on by another name; it clamps up to 1.
A comma and a percent in one frame. The checksum covers the ESCAPED bytes.
AUTH is the one duration with no lower clamp: 0 is how the buttons are disarmed.
The longest frame any named constructor can produce: two full-width arguments of entirely escapable bytes. 154 bytes, comfortably inside kMaxFrameLen.
A truncated relay command is worse than none, so a frame that will not fit emits ZERO bytes rather than a prefix.
The legacy message has nowhere to put a duration. This is the defect v2 exists to fix, and why the Mega's auto-off timer is independent of the bridge.
Identical bytes to encl-on-court-a, in the other direction. The collision is preserved on purpose: each end only ever reads one direction.
One staged row. !ROW never paints: !SHOW is what commits, so a half-written screen is never on the glass.
Twenty columns, the full width of the fitted 2004A. kMaxArgLen is 24, so the widest row still fits an argument.
A row carrying the frame's own delimiters. ',' and '%' escape; '*' does not need to, because the checksum delimiter is found by position from the end.
Commit the staged rows and hold them for ten seconds, flag bit0 asking for the countdown in row 3.
No screen may outlive two minutes. Clamped, never refused — the same rule ON's duration follows.
A zero hold would be a permanent screen wearing a timeout's clothes; it clamps up to one second, exactly as ON's zero clamps to kRelayMinSeconds.
The landing screen's row 3: bit0 WiFi up, bit1 API reachable, bit2 clock valid, bit3 restore pending — and the club's wall time.
WiFi up, API judged down, clock not trusted. A blank clock is honest; a stale one is not.
Relay index to the club's court number, so the glass can name the court the member is standing at.
Zero is unmapped: a box driving two courts renders the other two cells blank rather than as court zero.
The Mega's three since-boot counters ride the ping answer: frames it could not put on the wire, lines that did not decode, presses dropped with the window shut.
A Mega that has not been reflashed still answers with two arguments, and the bridge must still read it.
Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3). An optional third argument tags the frame; the Mega answers !ACK,<tag>,<code>. Sent only to a Mega that announced 3.x.
the duration still clamps to the hard cap; the tag is carried through untouched
Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3). Stage text into row 0 of screen 12 at column offset 0.
the second 24-character segment of a 48-character row (offset 24)

v3 reserves '!' as the frame sentinel on BOTH links, so a literal '!' in text is %21 — the Mega restarts a line on a bare '!'. A 2.1.0 Mega refuses %21, so the bridge never sends it one (it replaces '!' before encoding for a v2 Mega).
the same escaping applies to the v2 text verbs when a v3 encoder renders them

Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3). Commit screen 12: rows 0-3 (mask 15), hold 10 s, countdown flag, CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE of the staged rows (display/cases.json screen_crc).
the hold clamps into [1, 120] exactly as !SHOW
Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3). Relay reconcile: ensure A lit for at least 1800 s and D for 600 s; no opinion on B and C. Never opens a relay.
Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3). One Mega setting: LAYOUT 1 = expanded. Held in RAM only; a Mega boots compact.

Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3). Seconds of PAID light left per relay as the server's snapshot has it (chained extensions included); '-' = no figure, use the Mega's own deadline.
Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3). A landing note for 600 s, shown in the status slot.
Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3). Bridge liveness: expect the next frame within 5 s; the Mega declares the bridge dead after three periods of silence.
Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3). Uplink: tagged frame 7 applied.
uplink: screen 12 refused as incomplete (a row was missing or the CRC did not match); nothing was painted
Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3). Uplink, first frame after reset: version, MCUSR (08 = watchdog), keys held at boot (09 = A and D).
Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3). Uplink: keys A and D held together for 5 s inside the boot window — the setup-portal gesture.
Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3). Uplink after every !PONG: LCD timeouts, LCD re-inits, RX overruns, screen ceilings hit, authorisation-cap offs.

decode.note: Clamped, never rejected: a clamped light is a wrong-length game, a rejected one is a dark court.
Saturating, not wrapping. A value that overflows uint32 must become the hard cap, not a small number.
THE safety case. There is no ON frame without a duration, on the wire or in the API, so this line cannot become a relay command.
Round-trip of enc-lcd-escaped. A comma and a percent inside LCD text.
A malformed escape is rejected, not silently kept. Keeping it would break the round-trip and neither end could discover the disagreement.
Never guessed at: a half-understood relay command is worse than a missing one.
One flipped bit in the checksum field, which is the failure mode of 9600 baud next to four switching relay coils.
A truncated scanner code is a valid-looking code belonging to somebody else.
Two results here would mean every frame from a CRLF peer produced a spurious empty line.
How the UART actually delivers: half a frame this pass of loop(), the rest next.
Longer than kMaxFrameLen. Reported, and NOT parsed from the buffered prefix.
The over-long line looks like a valid ON prefix. It must not become one: the decoder resynchronises at the next terminator and the following frame is clean.
Blank lines are the gap between frames, not an error. Actual garbage is.
The spec says uppercase. Accepting lowercase would widen the set of byte sequences that count as a frame, and 'a' differs from 'A' by one bit.
Round-trip of enc-max-length-frame at the far end of the buffer.
A legacy on gets the hard cap, because the alternative is forever.

Two lines taken from Carl's sketch, not inferred from the command name. DENIED displays 'ACCESS DENIED', and two of the three carry a second line telling the player what to do. Decoding to the command text alone would show a member less than the hardware shows them today.

One legacy line, two v2 frames: the display, and the AUTH window that was implicit in Carl's sketch and had no expiry at all.
The same byte as decl-on-court-a, decoded in the other direction. This is the legacy collision the spec preserves rather than fixes.
The escaped delimiters survive the round trip byte for byte.
There is no row 4. Refused, never folded onto row 3: a row the panel does not have is a peer that disagrees about the hardware.
A row index is an index, not a quantity.
Twenty-five characters does not fit kMaxArgLen. Refused rather than truncated: half a message is a different message.
One frame delivered in three UART reads.
The two-minute clamp is the Mega's, applied on the way IN. No screen a bridge paints — including one from a firmware that does not exist yet — can persist past it.
The flags argument is not optional: a missing one read as zero would silently drop the countdown.
Four relays, four numbers. A short map would leave one court naming the previous tenant's number.
Two arguments still decode. The counters are additive, so a bridge flashed ahead of its Mega is not a bridge that stops hearing PONG.
Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3).
a 2.3.0 bridge never tags: the v3 Mega still takes the two-argument form
tags are 1-255; 0 would collide with "untagged"
one spelling per number

offsets are 0 or 24 only

%2A is accepted (never required: the checksum is the LAST '*')

a zero hold clamps up to 1, as !SHOW
a commit of no rows is not a screen
four UPPERCASE hex digits, like the frame checksum
Mega 3.0.0 / bridge 3.0.0 (docs/specs/device-serial-protocol.md, v3).
no opinion is spelled '-'; a zero would read as a one-second light once clamped
all four relays, always: a reconcile is a whole snapshot

an unknown key is well-formed: the Mega answers !ACK,4,2 (refused) and changes nothing
keys are 1-6 uppercase letters
values are 0-65535; the per-key clamp is the Mega application, not the decoder
